title: LEDGER: Budget-Bounded Generative Retrieval of Edit Demonstrations for Complex Instruction-Driven Image Editing
content: Instruction-driven image editing works well for a single change but collapses when a request contains several dependent steps: the strongest general systems score below 18 out of 100 on three-step chained instructions in ComplexBench-Edit, because a step is executed against a state that no longer matches its wording. Existing remedies decompose the request and re-call a multimodal model at every step, which multiplies inference cost and still re-derives every edit from scratch. We argue that the missing signal is the edit precedent: the same changes recur in real editing sessions, and a model that can look up how an atomic operation was carried out before does not have to re-infer it. We therefore treat complex editing as retrieval under a hard budget and propose LEDGER, which retrieves edit demonstrations with a generative late-interaction index. LEDGER encodes each demonstration into a short set of role tokens (operation, region, invariance) and scores them with role-weighted MaxSim, so the cost of matching is set by a token budget rather than by image resolution. A dependency graph over the request then allocates that budget across steps by marginal gain, and a residual gate re-queries only the stale region and invariance tokens after each step. On ComplexBench-Edit, LEDGER reaches 42.56 against 40.47 for a chain-of-thought baseline while reducing the drift on non-edited regions (L1 0.0542 versus 0.0595 for Gemini), transfers to MagicBrush single-turn edits (L1 0.0592, DINO 0.9031) and document revisions (total score 64.85 versus 58.77), and keeps the retrieval index at 84 MB for 40k demonstrations with 11~ms lookup, matching ColPali quality at a 16\( \times \) smaller index.
